questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: X is a crystalline sodium salt. Its aqueous solution turns litmus red and releases a gas that makes limewater milky when added to sodium carbonate. With barium chloride solution, X gives a white precipitate insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid. What is X?
questions.ai_explanation: Sodium hydrogensulfate, NaHSO₄, forms an acidic solution. Its hydrogen ions react with carbonate to release CO₂, which makes limewater milky. Its sulfate ions form insoluble white BaSO₄ with barium ions.
questions.explanation: Sodium hydrogensulfate, NaHSO₄, forms an acidic solution. Its hydrogen ions react with carbonate to release CO₂, which makes limewater milky. Its sulfate ions form insoluble white BaSO₄ with barium ions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Sodium chloride may be obtained from brine by
questions.ai_explanation: Evaporation removes water from brine. The dissolved sodium chloride remains and crystallises as enough water is lost.
questions.explanation: Evaporation removes water from brine. The dissolved sodium chloride remains and crystallises as enough water is lost.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The alkanol obtained from the production of soap is

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
In which of these reactions is iron oxidised?
1. Fe + H₂SO₄ → H₂ + FeSO₄
2. FeSO₄ + H₂S → FeS + H₂SO₄
3. 2FeCl₂ + Cl₂ → 2FeCl₃
4. 2FeCl₃ + SnCl₂ → 2FeCl₂ + SnCl₄
questions.ai_explanation: Oxidation means an increase in oxidation state. Iron changes from 0 to +2 in reaction 1 and from +2 to +3 in reaction 3. It remains +2 in reaction 2 and is reduced from +3 to +2 in reaction 4. Therefore, iron is oxidised in 1 and 3.
questions.explanation: Oxidation means an increase in oxidation state. Iron changes from 0 to +2 in reaction 1 and from +2 to +3 in reaction 3. It remains +2 in reaction 2 and is reduced from +3 to +2 in reaction 4. Therefore, iron is oxidised in 1 and 3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The flame used by welders in cutting metals is
questions.ai_explanation: Burning acetylene in oxygen produces the hot oxy-acetylene flame used for welding and cutting suitable metals. Oxygen alone is not a fuel.
questions.explanation: Burning acetylene in oxygen produces the hot oxy-acetylene flame used for welding and cutting suitable metals. Oxygen alone is not a fuel.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Consecutive members of an alkane homologous series differ by
questions.ai_explanation: Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Increasing n by one adds one carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms, so successive members differ by CH₂.
questions.explanation: Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Increasing n by one adds one carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms, so successive members differ by CH₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: If an element has the electronic configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p², it is
questions.ai_explanation: The final electrons occupy a p subshell (3p²), so the element belongs to the p block. The configuration contains 14 electrons and corresponds to silicon.
questions.explanation: The final electrons occupy a p subshell (3p²), so the element belongs to the p block. The configuration contains 14 electrons and corresponds to silicon.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
An organic compound X has relative molecular mass 180. It is a colourless crystalline solid, readily soluble in water, containing C, H and O in the atomic ratio 1:2:1. It has a sweet taste and melts on heating. In the presence of yeast and absence of air, X forms compound Y and a colourless gas. Y reacts with sodium to release gas Z, which gives a pop with a lighted splint. Y also reacts with ethanoic acid to form a sweet-smelling compound W.

Compound W is
questions.ai_explanation: Yeast converts glucose to ethanol, so Y is ethanol. Ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid to form ethyl ethanoate and water. Ethyl ethanoate belongs to the ester family, making W an ester.
questions.explanation: Yeast converts glucose to ethanol, so Y is ethanol. Ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid to form ethyl ethanoate and water. Ethyl ethanoate belongs to the ester family, making W an ester.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
An organic compound X has relative molecular mass 180. It is a colourless crystalline solid, readily soluble in water, containing C, H and O in the atomic ratio 1:2:1. It has a sweet taste and melts on heating. In the presence of yeast and absence of air, X forms compound Y and a colourless gas. Y reacts with sodium to release gas Z, which gives a pop with a lighted splint. Y also reacts with ethanoic acid to form a sweet-smelling compound W.

The molecular formula of X is
questions.ai_explanation: The atomic ratio gives empirical formula CH₂O, with formula mass 12 + 2 + 16 = 30. The molecular mass is 180, so the multiplier is 180 ÷ 30 = 6. The molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆.
questions.explanation: The atomic ratio gives empirical formula CH₂O, with formula mass 12 + 2 + 16 = 30. The molecular mass is 180, so the multiplier is 180 ÷ 30 = 6. The molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
An organic compound X has relative molecular mass 180. It is a colourless crystalline solid, readily soluble in water, containing C, H and O in the atomic ratio 1:2:1. It has a sweet taste and melts on heating. In the presence of yeast and absence of air, X forms compound Y and a colourless gas. Y reacts with sodium to release gas Z, which gives a pop with a lighted splint. Y also reacts with ethanoic acid to form a sweet-smelling compound W.

The reaction of X with yeast forms the basis of which industry?
questions.ai_explanation: Yeast ferments glucose without air to form ethanol and carbon dioxide: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. This process is central to brewing.
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments glucose without air to form ethanol and carbon dioxide: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. This process is central to brewing.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, which relationship connects pressure P, volume V and absolute temperature T?
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, PV = nRT. Rearranging gives P = nR(T/V). Since nR is constant, P is proportional to T/V, with T measured in kelvin.
questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, PV = nRT. Rearranging gives P = nR(T/V). Since nR is constant, P is proportional to T/V, with T measured in kelvin.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The colour imparted to a flame by calcium ion is
questions.ai_explanation: Calcium produces a brick-red (orange-red) flame. Sodium gives yellow, potassium lilac, and copper a blue-green flame.
questions.explanation: Calcium produces a brick-red (orange-red) flame. Sodium gives yellow, potassium lilac, and copper a blue-green flame.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In Fe + Cu²⁺ → Fe²⁺ + Cu, iron displaces copper from its ions because

options.A: iron is metallic while copper is ionic
options.B: the atomic weight of copper is greater than that of iron
options.C: copper metal has more electrons than iron metal
options.E: iron is higher in the electrochemical series than copper

questions.ai_explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper and more readily loses electrons. Fe is oxidised to Fe²⁺ while Cu²⁺ gains those electrons and becomes copper metal.
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper and more readily loses electrons. Fe is oxidised to Fe²⁺ while Cu²⁺ gains those electrons and becomes copper metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Sodium sulfate decahydrate (Na₂SO₄·10H₂O) loses water of crystallisation on exposure to air. This process is known as
questions.ai_explanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air. It differs from deliquescence, in which a solid absorbs enough moisture to dissolve.
questions.explanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air. It differs from deliquescence, in which a solid absorbs enough moisture to dissolve.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following happens during the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
questions.ai_explanation: At the anode, chloride ions lose electrons: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Loss of electrons is oxidation. At the cathode, sodium ions gain electrons to form sodium metal.
questions.explanation: At the anode, chloride ions lose electrons: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Loss of electrons is oxidation. At the cathode, sodium ions gain electrons to form sodium metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Crude petroleum pollution on creeks and waterways can be dispersed by

options.A: heating the affected water to boil off the petroleum
options.B: mechanically stirring to dissolve petroleum in water
options.C: pouring organic solvents into the water
options.E: cooling to freeze out the petroleum

questions.ai_explanation: Detergents contain surfactants that help break oil into small droplets dispersed in water. Dispersion does not destroy the oil; real spill treatment uses selected dispersants and considers environmental conditions.
questions.explanation: Detergents contain surfactants that help break oil into small droplets dispersed in water. Dispersion does not destroy the oil; real spill treatment uses selected dispersants and considers environmental conditions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Solutions X, Y and Z have pH values 3.0, 5.0 and 9.0 respectively. Which statement is correct?

options.C: Y and Z are more acidic than water
options.D: Y is more acidic than X

questions.ai_explanation: Higher pH corresponds to lower hydrogen-ion concentration. Z has the highest pH, 9.0, and is therefore the least acidic. X, with pH 3.0, is more acidic than Y, with pH 5.0.
questions.explanation: Higher pH corresponds to lower hydrogen-ion concentration. Z has the highest pH, 9.0, and is therefore the least acidic. X, with pH 3.0, is more acidic than Y, with pH 5.0.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Stainless steel is an alloy containing
questions.ai_explanation: Stainless steel is an iron alloy containing chromium and usually some carbon. Chromium forms a protective surface oxide that improves corrosion resistance.
questions.explanation: Stainless steel is an iron alloy containing chromium and usually some carbon. Chromium forms a protective surface oxide that improves corrosion resistance.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of 0.50 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ exactly neutralises 20 cm³ of 0.10 mol dm⁻³ NaOH?
questions.ai_explanation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. The NaOH amount is 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Half as many moles of H₂SO₄ are needed: 0.001 mol. Its volume is 0.001/0.50 = 0.002 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. The NaOH amount is 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Half as many moles of H₂SO₄ are needed: 0.001 mol. Its volume is 0.001/0.50 = 0.002 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A student prepares pure Cu(NO₃)₂ crystals starting with CuO. Which reported step is incorrect?

options.A: Some CuO was reacted with excess dilute H₂SO₄
options.C: After cooling, the crystals were separated by filtration
options.D: The crystals were washed with very cold water
options.E: The crystals were allowed to dry

questions.ai_explanation: Copper(II) nitrate requires nitrate ions. CuO reacts with nitric acid to form Cu(NO₃)₂ and water. Sulfuric acid would instead produce copper(II) sulfate, so step A cannot make the requested salt.
questions.explanation: Copper(II) nitrate requires nitrate ions. CuO reacts with nitric acid to form Cu(NO₃)₂ and water. Sulfuric acid would instead produce copper(II) sulfate, so step A cannot make the requested salt.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At 25 °C, 3.06 g of KClO₃ saturates 10 cm³ of water. Express the solubility in mol per dm³ of water. [K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16]
questions.ai_explanation: The formula mass of KClO₃ is 39 + 35.5 + 3×16 = 122.5. The dissolved amount is 3.06/122.5 ≈ 0.0250 mol in 10 cm³ of water. Per dm³ of water, this is 0.0250×100 = 2.50 mol.
questions.explanation: The formula mass of KClO₃ is 39 + 35.5 + 3×16 = 122.5. The dissolved amount is 3.06/122.5 ≈ 0.0250 mol in 10 cm³ of water. Per dm³ of water, this is 0.0250×100 = 2.50 mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The cracking process is very important in the petroleum industry because it
questions.ai_explanation: Cracking splits larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes. This increases the supply of shorter hydrocarbons useful in petrol and other engine fuels.
questions.explanation: Cracking splits larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes. This increases the supply of shorter hydrocarbons useful in petrol and other engine fuels.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which solution gives a white precipitate with barium chloride solution and a green flame test?
questions.ai_explanation: CuSO₄ contains sulfate ions, which give white BaSO₄ with barium chloride. Its copper ions produce a blue-green flame. Ammonium sulfate can give the sulfate precipitate but does not give the copper flame colour.
questions.explanation: CuSO₄ contains sulfate ions, which give white BaSO₄ with barium chloride. Its copper ions produce a blue-green flame. Ammonium sulfate can give the sulfate precipitate but does not give the copper flame colour.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The mass of an atom is determined by

options.D: the number of neutrons and protons
options.E: the number of neutrons and electrons

questions.ai_explanation: Almost all atomic mass comes from the nucleus. Protons and neutrons each have a mass close to 1 u; electrons contribute very little. The total number of protons and neutrons is the mass number.
questions.explanation: Almost all atomic mass comes from the nucleus. Protons and neutrons each have a mass close to 1 u; electrons contribute very little. The total number of protons and neutrons is the mass number.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. Which change greatly increases the rate of this reaction under otherwise identical conditions?

options.B: using a greater volume of acid
options.C: using a smaller volume of acid
options.D: placing the reaction vessel in an ice bath

questions.ai_explanation: Powdered zinc has a larger exposed surface area than the same mass in pellets. More zinc is in contact with the acid at once, so more successful collisions can occur per second.
questions.explanation: Powdered zinc has a larger exposed surface area than the same mass in pellets. More zinc is in contact with the acid at once, so more successful collisions can occur per second.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. How much zinc remains undissolved when 2.00 g of zinc reacts with 10 cm³ of 1.0 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄? [Zn = 65, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: The reaction is 1:1 in Zn and H₂SO₄. Acid supplied = 1.0×10/1000 = 0.010 mol, which consumes 0.010×65 = 0.65 g of zinc. The zinc remaining is 2.00 − 0.65 = 1.35 g.
questions.explanation: The reaction is 1:1 in Zn and H₂SO₄. Acid supplied = 1.0×10/1000 = 0.010 mol, which consumes 0.010×65 = 0.65 g of zinc. The zinc remaining is 2.00 − 0.65 = 1.35 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: NH₄NO₂ → N₂ + 2H₂O. What volume of nitrogen is produced from 3.20 g of ammonium nitrite at STP? Use a molar gas volume of 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹. [N = 14, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: NH₄NO₂ has formula mass 2×14 + 4×1 + 2×16 = 64. Its amount is 3.20/64 = 0.050 mol. The equation produces one mole of N₂ per mole of NH₄NO₂, so the nitrogen volume is 0.050×22.4 = 1.12 dm³.
questions.explanation: NH₄NO₂ has formula mass 2×14 + 4×1 + 2×16 = 64. Its amount is 3.20/64 = 0.050 mol. The equation produces one mole of N₂ per mole of NH₄NO₂, so the nitrogen volume is 0.050×22.4 = 1.12 dm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
Which of these elements will not react with either water or steam?
1. Carbon
2. Oxygen
3. Copper
4. Bromine
5. Zinc
questions.ai_explanation: Oxygen and copper do not react with water or steam in this comparison. Hot carbon and zinc react with steam. Bromine reacts reversibly with water to form HBr and HOBr, so copper and bromine cannot be the correct pair.
questions.explanation: Oxygen and copper do not react with water or steam in this comparison. Hot carbon and zinc react with steam. Bromine reacts reversibly with water to form HBr and HOBr, so copper and bromine cannot be the correct pair.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Naphthalene melts at 354 K (81 °C). At this temperature its molecules

options.E: become mobile as intermolecular forces holding the solid are overcome

questions.ai_explanation: On melting, naphthalene molecules gain enough energy to move out of their fixed crystal positions. The molecules remain chemically intact; it is the intermolecular attractions holding the solid structure that are overcome.
questions.explanation: On melting, naphthalene molecules gain enough energy to move out of their fixed crystal positions. The molecules remain chemically intact; it is the intermolecular attractions holding the solid structure that are overcome.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the ratio of the number of molecules in 2 g of hydrogen gas to that in 16 g of oxygen gas? [H = 1, O = 16]
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen is H₂: 2 g represents 2/2 = 1 mol of molecules. Oxygen is O₂: 16 g represents 16/32 = 0.5 mol. Molecule counts are proportional to moles, giving 1:0.5 = 2:1.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is H₂: 2 g represents 2/2 = 1 mol of molecules. Oxygen is O₂: 16 g represents 16/32 = 0.5 mol. Molecule counts are proportional to moles, giving 1:0.5 = 2:1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In which reaction does hydrogen peroxide act as a reducing agent?
questions.ai_explanation: A reducing agent is itself oxidised. In D, oxygen in H₂O₂ changes from −1 to 0 in O₂, while lead changes from +4 in PbO₂ to +2 in Pb(NO₃)₂. In the other reactions peroxide is reduced to water.
questions.explanation: A reducing agent is itself oxidised. In D, oxygen in H₂O₂ changes from −1 to 0 in O₂, while lead changes from +4 in PbO₂ to +2 in Pb(NO₃)₂. In the other reactions peroxide is reduced to water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Limewater, used to detect carbon dioxide in the laboratory, is an aqueous solution of
questions.ai_explanation: Limewater is a clear aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂. Carbon dioxide produces suspended calcium carbonate: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O, making it milky.
questions.explanation: Limewater is a clear aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂. Carbon dioxide produces suspended calcium carbonate: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O, making it milky.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which statement is not true of carbon monoxide under ordinary uncatalysed conditions?

options.B: CO is readily oxidised by air at room temperature to form CO₂
options.C: CO can be prepared by passing CO₂ over coke heated to about 1000 °C
options.D: CO can be prepared by heating charcoal with a limited supply of oxygen
options.E: CO is a good reducing agent

questions.ai_explanation: CO does not readily combine with air at room temperature without suitable activation or catalysis. It can burn to CO₂ when ignited. It is poisonous and can act as a reducing agent, so B is the false statement.
questions.explanation: CO does not readily combine with air at room temperature without suitable activation or catalysis. It can burn to CO₂ when ignited. It is poisonous and can act as a reducing agent, so B is the false statement.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: From ZnO + Na₂O → Na₂ZnO₂ and ZnO + CO₂ → ZnCO₃, zinc oxide may be classified as
questions.ai_explanation: Zinc oxide reacts with a basic oxide, Na₂O, and with an acidic oxide, CO₂. An oxide that can show both acidic and basic behaviour is amphoteric.
questions.explanation: Zinc oxide reacts with a basic oxide, Na₂O, and with an acidic oxide, CO₂. An oxide that can show both acidic and basic behaviour is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An example of a neutral oxide is
questions.ai_explanation: Carbon monoxide is classified as a neutral oxide in ordinary acid-base chemistry. CO₂, SO₂ and NO₂ are acidic oxides, while Al₂O₃ is amphoteric.
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is classified as a neutral oxide in ordinary acid-base chemistry. CO₂, SO₂ and NO₂ are acidic oxides, while Al₂O₃ is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In 3Cl₂ + 2NH₃ → N₂ + 6HCl, ammonia acts as
questions.ai_explanation: Nitrogen changes from −3 in NH₃ to 0 in N₂, so ammonia is oxidised. The substance that is oxidised reduces the other reactant and is therefore the reducing agent.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen changes from −3 in NH₃ to 0 in N₂, so ammonia is oxidised. The substance that is oxidised reduces the other reactant and is therefore the reducing agent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In the Haber process for manufacturing ammonia, finely divided iron is used as
questions.ai_explanation: Iron provides a catalytic surface that speeds up the reaction of nitrogen with hydrogen to make ammonia. It changes the rate of reaching equilibrium, not the equilibrium composition.
questions.explanation: Iron provides a catalytic surface that speeds up the reaction of nitrogen with hydrogen to make ammonia. It changes the rate of reaching equilibrium, not the equilibrium composition.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A compound has vapour density 56.5 relative to hydrogen and composition C 53.1%, N 12.4%, O 28.3%, H 6.2%. What is its molecular formula? [C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: Vapour density relative to hydrogen gives molecular mass 2×56.5 = 113. For 100 g, the approximate mole amounts are C:53.1/12, H:6.2/1, O:28.3/16 and N:12.4/14. Dividing by the smallest gives C:H:O:N ≈ 5:7:2:1. C₅H₇O₂N has formula mass 113, so it is also the molecular formula.
questions.explanation: Vapour density relative to hydrogen gives molecular mass 2×56.5 = 113. For 100 g, the approximate mole amounts are C:53.1/12, H:6.2/1, O:28.3/16 and N:12.4/14. Dividing by the smallest gives C:H:O:N ≈ 5:7:2:1. C₅H₇O₂N has formula mass 113, so it is also the molecular formula.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When a kerosene fraction from petroleum is heated strongly and converted into a lower-boiling liquid, the process is known as
questions.ai_explanation: Cracking uses heat, often with a catalyst, to break larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller ones. The smaller products generally have lower boiling points.
questions.explanation: Cracking uses heat, often with a catalyst, to break larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller ones. The smaller products generally have lower boiling points.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The compound CH₃CH₂C(=O)OH is
questions.ai_explanation: CH₃CH₂C(=O)OH contains a three-carbon chain ending in the carboxyl group, −COOH. The three-carbon carboxylic acid is propanoic acid, not propanol.
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂C(=O)OH contains a three-carbon chain ending in the carboxyl group, −COOH. The three-carbon carboxylic acid is propanoic acid, not propanol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Alkaline hydrolysis of naturally occurring fats and oils yields.
questions.ai_explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis breaks the ester bonds in fats and oils. It produces glycerol and the sodium or potassium salts of fatty acids, which are soaps.
questions.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis breaks the ester bonds in fats and oils. It produces glycerol and the sodium or potassium salts of fatty acids, which are soaps.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which formula represents a carboxylic acid? R denotes an organic group.
questions.ai_explanation: A carboxylic acid contains the −C(=O)OH group. A has this group; B is an ester, D an acid anhydride, and E an aldehyde. Sulfuric acid in C is not a carboxylic acid.
questions.explanation: A carboxylic acid contains the −C(=O)OH group. A has this group; B is an ester, D an acid anhydride, and E an aldehyde. Sulfuric acid in C is not a carboxylic acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The electricity needed to deposit 1 g of magnesium costs ₦5.00. At the same cost per unit charge and 100% current efficiency, what does it cost to deposit 10 g of aluminium? [Al = 27, Mg = 24]
questions.ai_explanation: Charge per gram is proportional to ionic charge divided by relative atomic mass. For 1 g Mg it is 2/24 mol of electrons; for 10 g Al it is 10×3/27 mol. The charge ratio is (30/27)/(2/24) = 13⅓. At the same cost per unit charge, the cost is ₦5×13⅓ = ₦66.67.
questions.explanation: Charge per gram is proportional to ionic charge divided by relative atomic mass. For 1 g Mg it is 2/24 mol of electrons; for 10 g Al it is 10×3/27 mol. The charge ratio is (30/27)/(2/24) = 13⅓. At the same cost per unit charge, the cost is ₦5×13⅓ = ₦66.67.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Nitrogen can best be obtained from a mixture of oxygen and nitrogen by passing the mixture over
questions.ai_explanation: Heated phosphorus removes oxygen by forming phosphorus oxide, leaving nitrogen. Magnesium is unsuitable because hot magnesium reacts with nitrogen as well as oxygen.
questions.explanation: Heated phosphorus removes oxygen by forming phosphorus oxide, leaving nitrogen. Magnesium is unsuitable because hot magnesium reacts with nitrogen as well as oxygen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Water is said to be ‘hard’ if it

options.B: must be warmed before sodium chloride dissolves
options.C: forms an insoluble scum with soap

questions.ai_explanation: Calcium and magnesium ions in hard water react with soap ions to form insoluble salts, seen as scum. This also makes it harder to obtain a lather.
questions.explanation: Calcium and magnesium ions in hard water react with soap ions to form insoluble salts, seen as scum. This also makes it harder to obtain a lather.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An aqueous metal salt M gives a white precipitate with NaOH, soluble in excess NaOH. It also gives a white precipitate with aqueous ammonia, soluble in excess ammonia. What is the cation in M?
questions.ai_explanation: Zinc ions form white Zn(OH)₂ with either reagent. The precipitate dissolves in excess NaOH because it is amphoteric, and in excess ammonia because zinc forms a soluble ammine complex. These two observations identify Zn²⁺.
questions.explanation: Zinc ions form white Zn(OH)₂ with either reagent. The precipitate dissolves in excess NaOH because it is amphoteric, and in excess ammonia because zinc forms a soluble ammine complex. These two observations identify Zn²⁺.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.ai_explanation: The longest continuous carbon chain has four carbon atoms, so the parent is butane. Numbering from the nearer end puts the methyl branch on carbon 2, giving 2-methylbutane.
questions.explanation: The longest continuous carbon chain has four carbon atoms, so the parent is butane. Numbering from the nearer end puts the methyl branch on carbon 2, giving 2-methylbutane.
